newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, Chechnya to discuss oil pipeline details.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Chechnya to discuss oil pipeline details.

text.p: Officials from Russia and breakaway Chechnya were expected to meet later on Saturday to discuss details of an agreement signed on Friday to transport Azeri oil in a pipeline crossing their territories.
Agreements on Russian-Chechen banking and customs relations were also on the agenda, officials said.

A duty officer in Russia's Fuel and Energy Ministry in Moscow said a ministry official would travel to the Chechen capital Grozny to meet Chechen officials. Russian Security Council officials were also expected to attend the talks.

The pipeline agreement, signed in the Azeri capital Baku, is important because Azerbaijan's pipeline into Russia goes through Chechnya, which has set itself up as a de facto independent entity after a bitter war with Moscow.

The deal, held up for months by bickering between the sides over details, could clear the way for crude output from an $8 billion Western consortium developing off-shore Azeri Caspian Sea fields to move through the pipeline to the Russian Black Sea port of Novorosssisk and on to world markets.
Few details of the agreement have been made public.

Radio Ekho Moskvy quoted a Chechen presidential aide on security, Akhmed Zakayev, as saying the agreement did not specify what tariffs Chechnya would get, but he said he did not expect any major further disputes.

"All questions were removed yesterday in the first half of the day in Moscow, and in Baku (Friday evening) we talked over all the nuances," he said. "On the whole, an agreement on all questions has been reached."
Chechen Interior Minister Kazbek Makhashev told Ekho Moskvy a supplementary agreement on tariffs and other details would take another 20 or 30 days.
He said that Russian special forces would guard the pipeline.

Friday's agreement was signed by Russian Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov, the president of Chechen state oil company YUNKO Khodzhakhmed Yarikhanov and the president of Azeri state oil company SOCAR.
The consortium, led by British Petroleum plc wants to begin using the route to transport its oil later this year.
